articleTitle: Behaviour of free conducting particles and their role on breakdown in oils under AC and DC voltages
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The experimental measurements of lift-off fields, transient currents, charge and discharge of spherical and cylindrical conducting particles are in good agreement with the theoretical predictions. The motions of these particles and their effects on prebreakdown and breakdown phenomena have been described. Cylindrical particles can reduce the AC breakdown voltage of uniform gaps to values as low as 20 kV/sub peak//cm. The breakdown voltage is significantly lower when the particle is free than when the particle is fixed. This is explained by an impulse-type breakdown from the particle tip generated by the particle/electrode micro-discharge rather than by a trigatron-type breakdown. The kind of experiment using a free particle is representative of critical situations that may appear in HV liquid insulated devices at large gaps.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling of conduction processes in dielectric liquids
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The simplest conduction model for gases subjected to ionization radiation was proposed by Thomson and Thomson (1928). This model was used by Adamchewski (1965), Malecki and Pieranski (1976) for theoretical description of ion conduction in dielectric liquids. The Thomson system of equations was reduced to dimensionless form convenient for model testing and numerical solution. This system of equations was obtained for transient and steady state conditions. Original models for description of electrohydrodynamic processes in dielectric liquids were proposed by Vartanyan et al. (1989) and Zhakin (1990). In these models of conduction the bulk and injection processes were included. On the basis of known theoretical data the authors proposed some results on theoretical and experimental investigation of conduction processes in dielectric liquids.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A relation between time-resolved discharge parameters and ageing
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: A study is described relating discharge data from large bandwidth electrical and optical measurements with ageing phenomena in polyethylene (PE) voids. Discharge-pulse shape, ignition voltage and spatial distribution of the discharge were monitored in disc-shaped voids during ageing. A link was made between the deposit of discharge by-products and the occurrence of minute discharge pulses by optical means. The electrical and optical parameters changed drastically during ageing and may be used as indicators for the stage of ageing that has been reached.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High temperature dielectric measurements on ceramics
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Results are presented of the dielectric properties at 2.45 GHz for several engineering ceramics over the temperature range 20 degrees C to 800 degrees C. An increase in the loss tangent is observed in some of these materials. In the case of zirconia there is some evidence to indicate a thermally activated conductivity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The surface phenomena of silicone rubber under the influence of impinging plasmas
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Surface characteristic properties of silicone rubber change under the conditions of a plasma impingement, especially the hydrophobicity. After a period of time, however, there is a certain amount of recovery of the water repellency. The object of the authors' work is to study the factors which influence this surface phenomena. It was found that the time duration of exposure to surface plasma, the corona intensive factor and the configuration of electrodes played some important part in the change of a sample's water repellency. The longer the time of exposure to the plasma, or the closer the distance of the sample surface to the plasma source, or the stronger the plasma intensity, the more severe was the decrease of the water contact angle on the sample surface. The lower the contact angle after plasma impingement, the higher was the relative recovery rate of the surface water repellency. The change of the surface chemical characterisation before and after the plasma impingement was detected. The possible reasons for the self-recovery of the surface hydrophobicity after exposure to plasmas are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quantitative measurement of mechanical stress in resins and its effect on electrical treeing
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The Shibuya fictive force model provides an appropriate method of estimating the sign and magnitude of the mechanical stress that occurs at the pin tip in pin-plane synthetic resin samples used to model electrical breakdown characteristics. The authors have illustrated how the quantifiable stress distribution along the pin axis direction in the pin/plane region modifies the breakdown characteristics and in particular shown how a region of zero stress can act as a barrier to tree growth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Statistical and fractal characteristics of simulated electrical tree growth
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Many aspects of electrical tree growth can be simulated by a model which neglects the microscopic degradation processes involved and models only the overall form of the tree and its interaction with the material and the applied field. The simulated trees generated by the model, like real electrical trees, have a distribution of propagation times to which the Weibull distribution can be applied. The characteristic value varies in a well defined way with the field exponent parameter governing the model. The degree of variation in propagation times in the model enables models in two and three dimensions to be interrelated. The fractal dimension of the tree structures is related to, and can be used to predict, the propagation time. It is also related to the degree of variation of propagation time. There is a possibility of using fractal dimensions of real electrical trees to predict the remanent life of insulation systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of artificial neural networks in discriminating partial discharge patterns
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: A novel alternative to statistical analysis is the use of artificial neural networks (ANNs). This paper investigates their use in recognising the PD patterns of solid-insulation test samples which contain a different number of cylindrical artificial voids. One of the aims is to determine whether such a technique is sensitive enough to detect the slight difference between these patterns. A typical three-layer network structure with feedforward connections is chosen together with the back-propagation learning method. The network used is also more complex with four output neurodes. Techniques to accelerate the training process of the neural network are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical fibre sensor for partial discharge detection and location in high-voltage power transformer
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: This paper investigates the possibility of applying a fibre optic sensor to detect the ultrasonic signals in HV power transformers. Since these signals are wide-band, the system should be able to detect the components in the low-frequency range. Descriptions of the operating principle together with the sensor construction and also the electronic circuitry necessary to process the optical signals are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Limitations on the damage mechanism in dry band arcing on all dielectric self supporting cables
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: A laboratory test has been developed that reproduces the dry band arcing failure mechanism seen under service conditions. The limitations of the test method have been investigated, and a range of test parameters defined within which dry band arcing is the failure mechanism. Comparison with a field trial has shown the similarities between the two, but by using an unrestricted current in the laboratory test, the dry down period is substantially reduced and arcing occurs after every wet/dry cycle. Additionally, the short duration, high current arcs produced add an additional damage mechanism that ensures the laboratory test is considerably more severe than a real installation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pulsed electroacoustic techniques to characterize charge accumulation properties
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The principle of the pulsed electroacoustic method is described. The acoustic pressure wave and the output voltage signal equations are described in the time and frequency domain, respectively. As an example, the time dependence of the space charge distribution in multi-ply polyethylene is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sheathing materials for dielectric, aerial, self-supporting cables for application on high voltage power lines
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The results from dry-band arc testing are strongly dependent on the test arrangements. In particular the impedance of the voltage source and supply circuit has a large effect. It is suggested that introducing a series resistor into the power supply in a salt-fog test may provide a useful technique by which such tests can be accelerated without recourse to use of unrealistically high voltages or short samples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A reassessment of the low temperature thermal degradation of cellulose
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Reviews the current knowledge of chemical degradation of cellulose and relate it to electrical insulation in oil-filled transformers. Paper impregnated with insulating oil is still widely used to insulate the windings of power transformers. A typical 600 MVA unit contains 12 t of paper and 45 t (40000 l) of oil.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Water-tree degradation in power cable insulation: understanding and prevention
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Illustrates how a combination of advanced analytical techniques, including electron microscopy, proton induced X-ray emission spectroscopy and micro-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy have been employed to establish the structure, composition and origins of water-treeing. Significant improvements in the performance of crosslinked polyethylene insulation can be achieved by applying a fundamental understanding of the physical and chemical origins of damage phenomena such as water-treeing. Certain features of water-treeing are highlighted and successful routes to improve the performance of polyethylene insulation discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assessment of insulation in aged power transformers by interfacial polarization spectrum and its correlation with chemical properties
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The ageing process of the paper can be monitored by measuring several properties such as tensile strength, electrical properties, degree of polymerisation (DP), furan content in the oil, return voltage measurement in the dielectric, etc. The DP technique has been widely studied by Shroff and Stannett. The cellulose fibres in paper degrade to produce a range of furans, some of which dissolve in the mineral oil. The correlation between the concentration of furans in the oil and the mechanical and dielectric properties of the paper has been studied. In the interfacing of the paper and oil in the transformer, interfacial polarization may occur, resulting an increase in the loss tangent and dielectric losses. A DC method was developed for measuring the interfacial polarization spectrum.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prebreakdown events in aromatic liquids
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The liquids preferred for high electric field applications are oils containing aromatic constituents or synthetic liquids such as alkyl-diphenyls. The authors test n-decane under DC and AC voltage and compared their results to those obtained in aromatic liquids (toluene and a constituent of a capacitor impregnant, benzyltoluene). The tip electrode was made by electrolytically etching a tungsten wire.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison of streamer and partial discharge inception voltages in liquid dielectrics
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: A study of three commercial liquids was undertaken and the results of this study are reported here. It is shown that the inception voltages for streamers and partial discharges are reasonably similar. It is suggested that the two phenomena are interrelated. The relationship between them is discussed in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interfacial breakdown phenomena between two EPDM surfaces
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The phenomenon of interfacial AC and DC breakdown is the subject of this paper. Two pieces of EPDM rubber were pressed together and a special jig was conceived so as to provoke arcing along the interface. The voltage at which breakdown occurred was measured and its dependence on the type of voltage (AC or DC), the interfacial pressure (0 to 100 kPa range) and on the presence of silicone grease was established. In the absence of silicone grease at the interface, DC breakdown voltages were two times greater than those for AC and both showed a linear dependence on pressure. With silicone grease, both AC and DC breakdown values were consistently higher; in the case of AC, values reached a plateau at higher pressures whereas for DC, values showed a slow linear increase with pressure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The influence of stray capacitance on wet tracking of polyester resin
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors investigated a means of possibly increasing the resistance to wet tracking. It is based on the supposition that dry band formation can be likened to the abrupt interruption of an electrical circuit by a switch. An arc is formed in this instance as in the breakdown of a dry band. It is proposed that methods used to suppress contact arcing and damage in a switch can be applied with equal validity to the suppression of dry band arcing and its damaging effect on surfaces. The energy in a switching transient can be removed from the sensitive contact breaker region by inclusion of capacitance. The influence of capacitance on wet tracking is investigated in the light of this equivalence.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Strong-field effects in disordered dielectrics with hopping conduction
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: It has been stated in a number of studies that the field dependence of differential conductivity in disordered dielectrics with hopping conduction has a minimum, an exponential rise in gamma (E) being preceded by a region of conductivity decline with increasing field strength Bottger and Bryksin (1985). The present pair shows that such a behaviour of the nonohmic hopping conductivity of disordered dielectrics is due to a change in charge transport paths and electronic density redistribution, and is inherent in systems with strong electron-phonon interaction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Space charge induced field variation on epoxy spacers under AC stresses in SF/sub 6/ (GIS)
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Large scale cylindrical spacers of commercial epoxy resin were used to have measured the charge accumulations under AC stresses. Using a finite-element program, the field variation due to the surface charges was calculated, and the influence of them on the dielectric performance was then discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Extension of life span of power transformer by on-site improvement of insulating oils
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The process described in this paper is the practical application of the concept that pre-emptive and preventative treatment on one or more occasions in the lifetime of a transformer can arrest the degradation of the insulation system-without removing the oil or even removing the transformer from the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric breakdown of ceramics and glass ceramics
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Discusses the AC dielectric breakdown of alumina, aluminium nitride and cordierite glass ceramics (MgO-Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/-SiO/sub 2/) at room temperature. The importance of specimen shape, thickness, surface finish and test conditions are assessed. For dielectric breakdown tests specimens were prepared in the form of 26 mm discs of various thicknesses (in the range 0.2-10.0 mm). In the case of alumina ceramics, plano-concave specimens were also prepared by diamond grinding one face to provide a curved surface (concave region 22 mm diameter, thickness at the centre 0.5-6.0 mm). The surface finish of the specimens ranged from as-received to 0.25 mu m diamond polished.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DC electrical characteristics of amalgamation regions in PE insulation
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Work is continuing to improve and enhance the reliability of moulded components. This paper reports on a study of flow patterns and morphology changes through the mould cavity with particular attention given to the amalgamation regions. DC breakdown data, together with preliminary findings of space charge measurements, are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The change of surface leakage current of composite insulators in salt-fog test
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The 1000 hours accelerated salt-fog ageing test has been used to determine the change of the hydrophobicity of HTV silicone rubber composite insulators by measuring the surface leakage current and observing the state of water repellency on the shed surface. The measured surface leakage current throughout the 1000 hours test is shown in the text. The leakage current was found to increase gradually from 10/sup -5/ A to 10/sup -2/ A. It was found that the degradation process of HTV silicone rubber composite insulators could be divided into four stages according to its surface leakage current, and each stage corresponds to different water repellent states of its shed surface.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The interpretation of Debye relaxation by means of a classical vibrational model
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Describes the motion in space and time of a dipole consequent upon the application of an electric field. The object of this paper is to provide an analysis of ideal Debye behaviour which is no more complicated than it needs to be, and which gives a physical picture of field dependent dipole motion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polarisation spectrum analysis for diagnosis of insulation systems
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The new method of test described in this paper is based on analysis of the polarisation spectrum traced from the results of Recovery Voltage Measurements. This method makes possible the assessment of oil/paper insulation systems such as in transformers. This new method is of significant importance as it is nondestructive and nonintrusive and gives full information on the state of oil/paper insulation systems. The condition of the paper is the decisive factor in the reliability of the overall system; high moisture content due to ageing or some external factor can cause failure as a result of increased dielectric losses at high temperature or release of moisture into the oil.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of hydrogen ions in electrolytic solutions on water tree growth in LDPE
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Hydrogen ion effects on water treeing were examined by adding small amounts of pure solution containing multi-valent cations or hydrochloric acid to a set of neutral univalent ionic solutions and used to grow water trees in LDPE. The effect of pure ionic solutions containing different valent cations were also studied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Barrier effect on electrical breakdown in nonuniform small and medium air gaps
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Examines the dielectric behavior of small and medium rod-rod air gaps with an insulating barrier, under lightning impulse voltages. The conclusions derived from the experimental investigation, refer to the influence of the gap length and the rod geometry to the breakdown voltage of the air gaps as well as to the definition of the optimum position of the insulating sheet.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The field dependence of electrical tree growth
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The field dependence of electrical tree lengths provides an accessible means of checking the applicability of the Dissado model (1989, 1990). The authors examine the ability of this model (in alternative versions) to reproduce the limited experimental data available. They show how the fractal nature of electrical trees can be used to avoid the complications involved in comparing data for trees of different shapes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterisation of amber defects in low density polyethylene insulation
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: As part of a research programme to examine the influence of controlled defects on the long term degradation mechanisms and life expectancy of polyethylene insulation a study has been carried out to characterise ambers and measure the short term impulse strength of standard LDPE samples with and without amber inclusions. Comparisons have also been made with samples containing inclusions of polyethylene which have either been thermally oxidised or exposed to gamma radiation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On-site loss tangent measurements of high voltage insulation
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors' work illuminates some problems encountered while on-site tests of high voltage insulation, especially such as that of measuring transformers. It has been proved that conventional, double-screened Schering bridge, operating with relatively low test voltage (e.g. 1-3 kV) can fulfil the requirements concerning the reliability of readings in high voltage environment, their broad interpretation, as well as in safety and manoeuvrability in operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bubble model of pulse breakdown in liquids
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The only form of generalization of experimental data on pulse breakdown in liquids now is empiric dependencies adaption. This paper is both an attempt at explanation of some dependencies and an attempt to clarify factors that determine discharge initiation. In submicrosecond range one can consider existing bubbles. So prebreakdown time lag and electrical strength of liquids are determined by factors that influence discharge initiation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On temperature dependence of electric strengths of polar polymeric films in low-temperature region
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: This paper describes the electrical breakdown of polar polymers especially in the cryogenic temperature region. The tests were made with newly developed specimens for the breakdown measurement at cryogenic temperature. The temperature dependence of electric strengths of polar polymeric films in the cryogenic temperature region is quite different from that reported previously with recessed specimens. The new results are inherent to the film. From the dependence of electric strength on the rise rate of applied field and prestressing, it is clear that the electrical breakdown of polar polymers at cryogenic temperature is affected by the space charge effect.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Water tree inception-experimental support for a mechanical/chemical/electrical theory
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The presence of water treeing degradation has been observed in most polymeric materials used as insulation in power cables. In this paper, a composite theory is proposed that describes a possible mechanism for tree inception and growth. As described here the theory relates to vented trees but it is reasonable to assume that a similar mechanism will be applicable to bow-tie trees. The theory seems to correlate well with existing data mainly concerning tree growth. New experimental data is presented which supports this theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Identification of PD sources in solids
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: It is of great importance not only to detect but also to localise and identify the source of partial discharges (PD). If the PD source type can be identified, it is possible to give a more reliable estimate of the potential damage. The authors present some general arguments for the acoustic mode density in cavities of different dimensionality: flat, hole or spherical. This knowledge may be utilised to identify the shape and size of a discharging cavity in solid insulators using the acoustic technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical signals from water trees-polarization and depolarization currents
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: If polymer insulated medium voltage cables are used in wet environments, after some time water trees are generated. As these objects may decrease the breakdown voltage, the interesting questions for utilities are, how many water trees exist in the insulation, what are their lengths and last but not least is there a risk for the safe operation of the cable. One chance to get some answers on these questions without digging out the cables is to apply an AC or a DC voltage to the cable and to measure the loss tangent, the shape of the AC current and/or the polarization and depolarization currents produced by the water trees. Comparing the different methods, the evaluation of the polarization and conduction currents produced by the water trees seems to be more sensitive than the change of the loss tangent, at least in the early stages of the water treeing phenomenon. Furthermore it is known that after termination of the voltage load, water diffuses out of the water trees and hence the electrical signals from water trees are decreased. To get a better understanding of these phenomena the authors aged commercial cable insulations in the laboratory under accelerating conditions (using a temperature gradient in the insulation), applied a DC voltage and analyzed the polarization and depolarization currents.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parameters for tree growth in cable insulation
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: One of the most interesting features of trees produced is the difference in the structure of the trees when several blocks of apparently identical material are compared. Another interesting feature is the sporadic growth of the trees. There can be periods of high growth rate interspersed with periods of slow growth followed by high growth rates again. Any attempt to successfully model the growth of trees must in some way be able to simulate these effects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of water treeing and the use of frequency acceleration techniques
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Discusses the life expectancy of a unit of insulation subject to water treeing and its assessment. There are a number of ways in which this can be done with acceleration relative to rated operating conditions. One method consists of time to failure (breakdown) tests for a number of samples for each of several acceleration factors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Space-charge and breakdown in artificial tree channels
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Auckland et al (1974) were among the first to consider that the electric strength of an electrical tree channel could be high; indeed comparable to that of the surrounding solid dielectric. Their results showed that the electric strength of air in a confined channel increased as the channel diameter decreased below 200 mu m. These observations were explained in terms of the avalanche theory in which the diffusion of electrons as the avalanche advances produces a conically shaped volume of negative charge with its apex at the cathode. For long or narrow channels, the head of the avalanche comes into contact with the channel walls. The role of trapped charge was conjecture on the part of Auckland et al. The authors correct this deficiency and investigate the part played by the trapped charge in the process of tree growth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Water treeing in XLPE
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Water treeing in underground HV power cables initiates in all solid dielectric materials from sites of high electrical stress such as rough interfaces, protruding conductive points, voids or imbedded contaminants. Water treeing is characterized by: (1) foundation of moisture or water is essential for the water growth; (2) water treeing can grow in the underground cables for years before reaching a size where it may contribute to breakdown; (3)the applied voltage required for water treeing initiation is much lower than that required for the development of electrical trees, and (4) the growth of water trees is accelerated under frequency, no water trees generate under DC voltage. It was reported that at frequencies from 6 kHZ to 10 kHZ trees could be grown in less than 30 days which would normally have required years to grow under service conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A practical life assessment technique for aged oil paper systems
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: A significant percentage of the transformer population is now aged beyond a nominal design life of 25 to 30 years. As much of this equipment is performing quite satisfactorily, economic factors usually favour continued operation for as long as possible. The operating environment in which the following studies were undertaken is an extensive transmission system operating at voltages up to 275 kV. The climatic conditions are tropical and subtropical, which are conducive to the ageing mechanisms of oil impregnated paper insulation. The author studies insulation condition monitoring and life assessment techniques. One research project has been particularly useful in providing a practical method for estimating the remaining reliable life of ageing power transformers employing oil/paper insulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling of space charge relaxation under the conditions used for thermally stimulated discharge current measurements
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors investigate the forms of TSDC spectra produced by a computer model based on charge migrating through a dielectric by a hopping mechanism. The activation energy of the process is calculated from the spectra and the deviations from expected behaviour are noted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparative study of water tree growth in low density polyethylene aged in different electrolytes
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Water treeing in polymeric power cables is an important concern to manufacturers. Research to date has not clarified the mechanism but two factors regarded as important are oxidation and ion penetration. The present work reports studies performed on low density polyethylene (LDPE) aged in different electrolytes to determine if there is any relationship between these factors and water tree growth. Experimental techniques used were Fourier transform infra red (FTIR) spectroscopy, neutron activation analysis (NAA), thermally stimulated creep (TSCr) and DC conductivity measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Progress with polymeric insulators on British Rail
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Polymeric insulators have been in use on British Rail (BR) overhead lines for 20 years. Their flexibility, small diameter and low mass make them attractive for use in areas such as section insulators, bridges and tunnels of tight clearance and in areas of vandalism. Some designs in the past have given problems, such as poor track resistance, poor coating adhesion, or notching of glass fibre rod, but after a long materials evaluation and with production to improved specifications, the polymeric insulator is now the most reliable insulator in service. In the last decade these polymeric materials have been introduced into other areas of railway equipment, and have performed well.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Image analysis of electrical trees
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: This paper presents an automated technique for monitoring the growth of electrical tree structures. Each stage of the propagation is recorded and the images analysed to give a series of measured and calculated values. Electrical tree growth was investigated using epoxy resin samples with point-plane electrodes. The test and material parameters were controlled or measured accurately for reproducibility. A point-plane separation of 2 mm and applied voltage of 10 kVrms were used throughout the tests.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dissipation factor and water treeing of WTR-XLPE cable insulation
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Tests three commercially available water tree retardant XLPE materials (WTR) and compares some of their properties with conventional XLPE insulation. The authors have focused on water treeing and dissipation factor. Water tree tests have been performed on Rogowski type test objects at room temperature ( approximately 20 degrees C), energized by an AC stress of approximately 10 kV/mm, for up to nine weeks of ageing ( approximately 1500 hours). This paper shows that water trees are initiated also in WTR-materials and their growth rates are approximately as for conventional XLPE. It is also shown that mechanical strain eases both initiation and growth of water trees. In particular one of the WTR-materials was significantly more affected than the other materials.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Condition monitoring of the stator winding insulation of HV electrical air cooled rotating plant
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors discuss the condition monitoring of the high voltage stator insulation of air cooled generators and large AC electric motors. Some of the diagnostic techniques applicable are briefly described and their capability assessed. A philosophy for condition monitoring is proposed and examples of their application are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigations of degradation of XLPE insulation in low voltage aerial bundle cable systems
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Aerial bundle cable (ABC) systems were introduced in Australia in 1985 for low voltage reticulation. Although ABC systems had been reported to have been operated successfully for many years in Europe and Scandinavia, potential degradation problems could be caused in Australia by extreme climatic conditions and the use of insulating materials that are not proven for Australian conditions. This paper describes preliminary results from a research project aimed at identifying degradation processes in Australian ABC systems. The project has two major components: a chemical evaluation of degradation of the polymeric materials in ABC systems (particularly XLPE) and an engineering investigation into the long-term behaviour of the overall system including supports and connectors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of physical ageing of polymers on dielectric permittivity and loss values over wide temperature and frequency ranges
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Ageing of polymeric materials such as PS, PVC, PET occurs strongly in the region of the low temperature tail of the alpha a relaxation process. This ageing process increases the dynamic modulus, decreases dynamic mechanical and dielectric tan delta , but has little effect on the dielectric constant. The major effect of ageing is the reduction in mobility with depression of the relaxation spectrum related to the ageing time and temperature.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharge testing of unshielded cables
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The power, control, and instrumentation cables can be critical components of a plant life extension program, especially for nuclear stations. However, in many situations, especially for older plants, the cables are unshielded. A major challenge in applying diagnostic tests to these cables is the lack of a well-defined, stable ground plane. In recognition of this difficulty, recent work at Ontario Hydro has sought to determine whether an adequate ground plane for testing such cables can be defined. Analytical and experimental studies have been carried out into the feasibility of grounding adjacent conductors to form a testable configuration. The results of impedance analyses and numerical calculations of the electric field distribution using finite element techniques have shown that a ground plane, although not completely uniform, can be formed using this method. Partial discharge was detected with high probability on unshielded cables in which adjacent conductors were grounded.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling space charge and field in solid dielectrics
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The complex mechanisms which cause the high-voltage breakdown of solid dielectrics are currently being studied by a collaborative project in the UK. Fundamental to the understanding of breakdown is mathematical modelling of the macroscopic motion of charge in a dielectric under high field. This paper draws together some of the results obtained from the modelling. Validation of Deutsch's assumption (1933), which underlies the work, and results corresponding to an a.c. applied voltage are presented for the first time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prebreakdown cavities in viscous silicone fluids and their relationship to initiating current pulses
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The mechanism of electrical breakdown in liquid dielectrics is slowly being revealed. Two basic processes have been discerned: one is a fast electronic process that occurs within the liquid itself; the other is a much slower process involving the production and growth of a vapour cavity. The authors focus on the fast pulses that are responsible for the initiation of negative point discharges, and on the initial growth of the resulting pre-breakdown vapour cavities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The dielectric response of a commercial polyhydroxybutyrate biological polymer
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors present measurements of complex relative permittivity for poly- beta -hydroxybutyrate homopolymer over the ranges 0.1 Hz to 3 MHz and -175 degrees C to +145 degrees C.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ferroelectric ceramic/polar polymer composite films for pyroelectric sensors
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Discusses a polymer/ceramic composite, in which a fine ceramic powder is dispersed in a polymer matrix. This paper focuses on the relevant properties of composites that make them suitable for their use in pyroelectric detectors, using the pyroelectric figure of merit defined as p/ epsilon ( mu C/m/sup 2/K). The authors report the results for the pyroelectric and dielectric properties of composites made with a polymer, P(VDF/TrFE) and various ferroelectric ceramics such as PZT, PLZT, and Ca modified PT. PLZT ceramic was chosen as a ceramic dispersoid because of its high resistivity when compared to other ferroelectric ceramics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of oil quality after chemical destruction of PCB's in transformers
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Many mineral transformer oils contain contaminant PCB's at low levels (generally less than 1000 ppm). This contamination occurred during bulk transport. International standards and inter-government agreements (eg North Sea Conference in 1991) will limit permitted contamination to no greater than 50 ppm. Since mineral oil resources for napthenic grade transformer oil are limited and removal of PCB's are the objective, the technology of chemical dechlorination of PCB's while simultaneously reclaiming the mineral oil was investigated along with PCB removal alternatives. This process known as 'PCB-Gone' is moderate in its reaction yet very effective in destruction of the PCB molecule.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The influence of morphology on space charge accumulation
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors report on a preliminary study of the influence of morphology on space charge accumulation in polymer insulators. To illustrate the space charge measurement principle, bulk charge and the associated electric stress distributions in a low density polyethylene sample after high electrical stressing are presented. Two samples of polypropylene film with different morphology have also been produced by appropriate thermal treatment. The morphologies of the two polypropylene samples were characterised using the permanganic etching technique. Transmission electron micrographs of the two samples are presented. Measurements of the bulk charge distribution and associated electric stress profiles for the two morphologies are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aromatic polyimides with low dielectric constant
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Discusses the synthesis and characterization of fluorine containing polyimides and elaborates a structure/property relationship. Furthermore the authors employed molecular modelization in order to understand and predict properties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Discharging and thermally stimulated polarization (TSP) currents in aromatic polyamides
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Discharging current measurements are reported in aramid paper over a wide range of temperatures and electric field strengths. The results show that at lower temperatures dipolar polarization occurs. With increasing temperature there is increasing contribution from interfacial polarization and at 200 degrees C the latter mechanism is predominant. Measurement of thermally stimulated polarization currents supports the proposed mechanism. By separating the dipolar polarization currents from interfacial polarization currents additional evidence has been obtained for the proposed mechanism. An activation energy of 0.84 eV is obtained for the dipolar process. On the basis of Debye theory a relaxation time of 6.3*10/sup 4/ s is obtained at 30 degrees C.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new tool for the assessment of fire performance of synthetic materials used as insulation cable the EDF/CNRS calorimeter
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Describes a new calorimeter that allows heat release rate measurements with two techniques. The main contribution is related to the thermal method since convective and radiative components can be measured simultaneously. Hence, the usual limitation due to heat losses is overcome and the accuracy of the thermal and oxygen methods can be compared directly. For the main part, this comparison will be based on measurements performed with a gas burner fed with methane. However, to check the ability to measure heat release of solid materials, the results obtained with polymethylethacrylate (PMMA) and polyvinylchloride (PVC) are considered as well.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated creep spectroscopy as a method to characterize ageing in insulating materials
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Insulating polymeric materials are generally semicrystalline. Upon metastability of the amorphous phases, the properties of polymeric materials change with time if the temperature is lower than the glass transition. This spontaneous ageing is characterized by an endothermic phenomenon in differential scanning calorimetry and must be distinguished from the stimulated ageing caused by modifications of physical and/or chemical bonds caused for instance by electric stress or environmental conditions. These modifications affect fundamentally the molecular mobility of the disordered phases (paracrystalline domains, rigid amorphous domains and the true or free amorphous phase). The process by which the molecules rearrange is characteristic of the structure and the morphology of polymers. So the quantitative study by thermally stimulated creep spectroscopy (TSCr) of its kinetic can be used to quantify the ageing procedure. The TSCr spectroscopy is applied to the study of low density polyethylene (LDPE) in the temperature range -180 degrees C/80 degrees C.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical fibre line current measurement system
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Optically coupled current measurement systems obviate the need for the large amounts of insulation required in high voltage CTs and usually allow the sensor to be sited hundreds of metres from the receiving end. The sensor described in the paper uses less power than previously reported hybrid systems which allows operation from a minimum line current of 3A rms. Chromatic modulation is used in which a continuous wide range of wavelengths is used with the measurement information encoded on the spectral signature of this optical signal. The advantages of the chromatic modulation technique include intensity independent modulation, high optical efficiency and high sensitivity. The block diagram of the current measurement system is shown. A broad band light source is used to optically activate the system. This light source addresses liquid crystal elements via an optical fibre.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric measurements of glasses by 21 GHz during the annealing
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: A dielectric measurement instrument at 21 GHz was arranged for investigation of the influences of the structure relaxation on the dielectric properties of glasses. Some phosphate crown and fluorine crown glasses are measured. The time-dependent change of dielectric constant was observed during annealing. A double potential model is used to interpret this effect.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Diagnostic techniques for the field evaluation of polymer concrete insulators
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Several diagnostic techniques were employed in order to develop a methodology to evaluate the field performance of polymer concrete pin type insulators. These will be installed in the UK overhead distribution network under various weathering and pollution conditions. The techniques used include measurements such as surface roughness, water contact angle, surface resistance under clean fog conditions and flashover voltage under artificial pollution conditions. Results of these measurements are given for new and aged insulators. From the results, it is concluded that the evaluation methodology is a valuable tool for diagnosis of the effect of surface changes on the electrical performance of polymer concrete insulators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical characterisation of a single creeping streamer in transformer oil
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The use of capacitive probes is of great interest for determining the electrical characteristics of the creepage discharges, and should contribute to a better understanding of the streamer propagation mechanisms. The first results on space and time variation of electric potential along the quasi-rectilinear streamer indicate that the streamer is not equipotential; there is a finite potential gradient along the channel which apparently increases when going from the needle to the tip of the streamer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharge recording & analysis
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Partial Discharge (PD) has become an important tool in the assessment of electrical insulation. In particular, it appears to be one of the few methods that has any hope of predicting remnant life of any particular piece of equipment. Such predictions hinge on changes in the discharge pattern over the lifetime of the equipment. The present paper describes a method of recording the PD activity which measure individual discharges and the point-on-cycle (POC) at which they occur. The circuit involves a varying level of sensitivity rather than a set dead-time usually employed to separate discharges. This means that large pulses are not prevented from being registered by a prior smaller discharge.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Photoconductive switch design and applications
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: In the high-voltage area many new applications have resulted from utilizing photoconductive switches, such as the high-voltage analogue waveform generator, the distributor-less car ignition system, the HV-impulse generator, the voltage limiting surge arrestor, etc, where the photoconductive devices offer comparable advantages in terms of high-dielectric breakdown strength, high-current capacity, large dynamic range, 'jitter-free' response and bilateral conduction characteristics. This paper reviews the photoconductive switch design and applications, including the recent development of the power photoconductive switch, and evaluates the advantages provided by photoconductive switches over conventional electronic devices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Studies of partial discharges in HV machines: initial considerations for a PD specification
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The search for a low attenuation region for discharge measurements, which is fundamental to setting a discharge acceptance level for machine stators, is promising. One uncertainty is over winding resonance effects and it is proposed to undertake a major investigation over a wide range of machine sizes to assess this effect. Calibration of the discharge measuring arrangement in terms of apparent discharge magnitude is critical to obtaining comparable and repeatable results. The IEC method has been examined experimentally to determine the effects of calibration source impedance and has been found to be satisfactory. No significant high frequency magnetic coupling of discharge pulses was observed. Radiation effects can be significant and must be reduced to an acceptable level so accurate measurements can be made.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of measuring techniques used in evaluating the insulation condition of large turbogenerator rotor windings
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors briefly illustrate the main measuring methods currently developed and standardized by ENEL to search for insulation faults between turns. Such a category of faults is more insidious for the continuity of service because it is not directly detectable from the protection system during operation. The information obtained through impedance and reflectometric measurements supplies sufficient data to ascertain the existence and location of the fault. However these are not reliable enough to measure the actual state of degradation of the fault. All this has shown the need for further testing methods whose results could have a direct correlation to the actual energy lost by the fault during operation. This is the aim of recent experimentation on the spectral content of the shaft voltage.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Acoustic and dielectric losses in pure and doped Bi/sub 12/SiO/sub 20/ (BSO) single crystals
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Doping of Bi/sub 12/SiO/sub 20/ (BSO) single crystals by cations of 2- and 3- valence metals is common to control their properties. But the real defect structure of BSO has not been studied completely. This report shows the results of application of internal friction method in combination with dielectric and electric measurements to investigate defects occurring in crystals after doping by Cr, Al and annealing in vacuo.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calculation of inception voltages in SF/sub 6/-N/sub 2/ mixtures
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: A simple method to calculate the breakdown voltage of SF/sub 6/-N/sub 2/ and SF/sub 6/-air and SF/sub 6/-N/sub 2/-Air mixtures at different percentage of SF/sub 6/ in the mixture is developed over a wide range of Pd(100<Pd<12000 Torr.cm). The breakdown voltages of SF/sub 6/-gas and SF/sub 6/-gas mixtures are in close agreement with the measured values.<<ETX>>

articleTitle: Arc-control devices for use on all-dielectric, self-supporting, optical cables
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: All-dielectric, self-supporting, optical cables strung on power transmission lines can suffer from electrical degradation, which is now generally acknowledged to be caused by dry-band arcing. The author shows that arc-control devices are a credible line of enquiry in the search for methods of preventing dry-band arcing damage on self-supporting optical cables, and have a reasonable chance of success.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric relaxation spectrometry of polymeric solids
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The dielectric properties of a range of carbonyl-containing polymers have been investigated using the wideband capacitative-T permittivity bridge of Pratt and Smith (1982). The bridge provides multi-point data over a range of relaxation maxima. Four applications are presented which illustrate the utility of the dielectric method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The curing of epoxy/amine systems viewed through microdielectrometry
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Show how microdielectrometry can improve the curing of epoxy resins by detecting real-time critical events like gelation or vitrification. The study is based on a well-known system (DGEBA/3DCM in stoichiometric proportions) in order to clearly distinguish the two principal phenomena observed during the curing, which are gelation and vitrification.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The location of the pre-breakdown region in a cross-linked polyethylene insulated cable
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Cables containing water trees have some detectable discharges prior to breakdown. Indeed, the lower the breakdown strength the longer the period of discharging before breakdown. A cable containing water trees provides a sample which is likely to have discharging sites prior to breakdown. This paper describes how a discharging site was monitored, located and examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time-domain dielectric relaxation in PMMA and NBR
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Time-domain dielectric relaxation (after-effect) was studied using samples of PMMA and NBR subjected to a voltage step of 100 V (rise time 3 mu s). The response curves consisted of a transient dipole reorientation part followed by a conduction stage. After separation of the two contributions the transient response was fitted to a stretched exponential and the value of its exponent determined. The primary aim of the measurements was to compare the values of beta in the stretched exponential exp(-kt/sup beta /) with those describing mechanical stress relaxation, where for a number of solids with varying structure and composition, including both polymers and metals, beta approximately=0.27+or-10% has been reported. For PMMA agreement with the latter value was found within a temperature range varying from -5 degrees C to +32 degrees C, that is well below T/sub g/. With NBR similar values of beta were found only at relatively low temperatures (-25 degrees C to -30 degrees C). There was a distinct increase in beta with temperature for both polymers. The time-domain spectrometry allowed the data to be converted into the corresponding frequency response.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On data analysis and processing of partial discharge pulses using software orientated techniques
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The detection of partial discharge activity from the solid insulating systems of high voltage plant is well-recognised as a measurement whose interpretation can prove valuable in the assessment of insulation integrity. Partial discharge detectors have traditionally been configured to display the pulses from the partial discharges superimposed on the AC power cycle. Knowledge of these pulse amplitudes, their phase distribution, polarity and overall number per cycle can be used, often in conjunction with the knowledge of how these parameters vary with applied voltage and, at a fixed applied voltage, with time, to provide a valuable insight into the nature, extent and location of degradation sites within the solid insulating system. Given the plethora of parameters to be measured and presumed necessity for accuracy and objectivity, it is not surprising that digital technology has been utilised to this end and many such systems are now being reported in the literature. Indeed, the data manipulating power of such systems is now producing results which indicate that more complex pattern changes can be analysed to provide increasing sophisticated assessments relating to insulation integrity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Discharge magnitude distribution and discharge luminescence in an electrical treeing (Polarity effects for prediction of tree initiation)
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors investigate how to improve the prediction of tree initiation by the polarity effects indicated in the discharge magnitude distributions. This work measures particularly the negative discharge pulses in addition to positive. During sample heating, a steel needle electrode (diameter:1 mm) was inserted into polymethylmethacrylate. The experimental samples consisted of an artificial fine void (length:1.5 mm) with air at 1 atm. The test voltage was AC 50 Hz, 14 kV. The discharge magnitude, the discharge luminescence and the tree configurations were measured and observed until 30 minutes after the tree initiation. The experimental procedure was carried out at room temperature in silicone oil and 30 samples were tested.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simultaneous thermal and infrared analysis of insulating resins
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: This paper gives details of the use of the simultaneous thermal and infrared analysis (TGA/IR) technique as part of the assessment of the degradation of an unsaturated polyester resin used in long term electrical breakdown tests. Results are presented showing the correlation between weight loss, temperature and chemical species.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement of the relative complex permittivity at microwave frequencies by an improved short-circuit (ISC) method
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Among microwave methods for the measurement of complex permittivity of dielectric materials are the 'transmission-line type' methods. The principle of the short circuit method is shown. The measurements are performed on the standing wave in front of dielectric sample in a slotted waveguide. In this paper a new variant named 'improved short-circuit' (ISC) method is described; also, experimental results on 'polyamide-66' samples are reported and a detailed analysis of the total relative errors is performed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A multifactor stress ageing model of electrical insulation
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The single stress approach in design stage and also in ageing studies offers relative simplicity, but it is inapplicable to real life operating conditions which mostly are of multistress type. The article presents a generalized model for the electrical equipment design using the multistress approach. The generality of the model lies in the fact that it can be used for designing of insulation system of all electrical components containing solid insulating materials surrounded by gas or liquid insulation or impregnated by them. At the same time, the model enables simultaneous consideration of the influences of different stresses when those loads appear as constant, variable and stochastic inputs. Besides, the inherent physical and chemical properties of the insulating materials used are also included in the model. This enables, when the changes of those properties with the operating time are known, the ageing process to be introduced in the model itself.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the correlation between partial discharge parameters and the degradation characteristics of polyester resin insulating systems
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: If trends in measured discharge data can be correlated with the breakdown process then there exists a possibility for the development of on-line breakdown prediction techniques. The use of automated test and measurement allows making twelve related measurements on experimental samples as degradation 'trees' are initiated and grow to final complete breakdown of the material. Correlations between these measurements are found and conclusions are drawn with regard to the significance of certain measurements and their effectiveness for breakdown prediction. The sample material was transparent polyester resin with point-plane electrode geometry. The electrode gap was 2 mm. All experiments were conducted with the plane electrode grounded and 10 kV, 50 Hz a.c. applied to the embedded needle.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of dielectric properties on the basis of a non-conventional measuring procedure
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors' work deals with a new procedure for evaluation of the properties of dielectric materials. It is based on a modified bridge circuit for measurement the total charge of partial discharges under AC stresses. In order to apply this method for practical investigations on HV components, a prototype of a dielectric analyzer (DIANA) was developed. Preliminary test results showed that knowledge on dielectric behaviour of electrical insulation can be increased essentially by the new method, compared to the classical power loss factor measurement. Because of the time resolved display of the capacitive and resistive voltage vector even nonlinear phenomena may be detected.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling of the reflection of an open-ended coaxial line and its use for accurate complex permittivity measurements at frequencies up to 20 GHz
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: An open-ended coaxial line can be used as a sensor in nondestructive dielectric measurements. The technique is based on the study of the fringing field of an open-ended coaxial line and its perturbation by a lossy dielectric. The open end of the coaxial line is terminated by the sample material and the input reflection coefficient of the sensor is measured using a network analyzer. A number of models have been developed in order to relate these data to the complex permittivity of the material. The equivalent circuit model was shown to be suitable only up to a few gigahertz, particularly for lossy dielectric measurements. In this paper, a comparison is made between two different formulations which allow the complex permittivity of the terminating material to be derived from the reflection coefficient of a coaxial sensor. It is found that there is a systematic difference between the values of aperture admittance predicted by the two models. When a calibration procedure was performed at the measuring end of the probe, the two models were found suitable for accurate dielectric measurements up to 20 GHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The lightning impulse breakdown characteristics of oil gaps between wire-disks in 500 kV transformer windings
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The experiment and research results of lightning impulse breakdown characteristics of oil gaps between winding disks of a 500 kV power transformer is described in this paper. Based on the analyses of the electric field of the interleaved type disks the test models which reflect the feature of combined electric field were designed and the step up test method was used to test the models. The research of probability distribution showed that the lightning impulse breakdown voltage of oil gap between winding disks is distributed as the normal distribution and the experimental data were processed according to the maximum likelihood principle to obtain the 50% breakdown voltage and the standard deviation of some models with various sizes. The research results showed that the narrow oil gaps between wire-disks could be used to replace the wide one and the axial height of the windings might be decreased about 10%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The electrokinetic properties of metal-dielectric interfaces
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors describe a sensitive interferometric system capable of measuring mechanical displacements at dielectric-metal electrode interfaces when subjected to alternating electric fields as weak as 0.1 V mm/sup -1/. They show that, for a number of dielectric-metal interfaces, the displacements have a significant component at the fundamental frequency of the applied field, f, and, when the field is low, a weaker component at 2f. They suggest that the results can be explained most conveniently in terms of the Gibb's adsorption equation for the interface which relates the interfacial energy to the electrical properties of the double layer established at the dielectric-metal contact. The implications of these electrokinetic results for situations of practical importance will be discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Traceable dielectric measurements by resonance methods in the frequency range 1-30 MHz
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
