abstract: It is shown that traceable Q measurements on a stable inductor can provide the basis for dielectric measurements in the frequency range 1-30 MHz. It is also possible to adapt computer controlled four terminal impedance measuring techniques by coupling them with a resonance adaptor and suitable test fixture, so that dielectric measurements may be made to +or-2% in permittivity and +or-5 mu rad in dielectric loss.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Surface processing of PTFE by electrical discharge under high E/N conditions
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors investigated the mechanism of gas discharges under high E/N conditions. From the result, it is predicted that many activated species are generated in the ionized space by the Monte Carlo simulation. For example, many ions with kinetic energy larger than 100 eV are expected. Gaseous discharge under high E/N conditions is effective to improve surface properties of polymers. The authors are interested in chemical and/or physical functions on the PTFE surface, one of the most stable polymers, in view of not only chemistry but also to extend the electrical application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microwave dielectric ceramics in the system ZrO/sub 2/-TiO/sub 2/-SnO/sub 2/
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: In this study ceramics of composition Zr/sub 0.8/Sn/sub 0.2/TiO/sub 4/ have been prepared by the mixed oxide route using different divalent and trivalent mixed oxide additives. The effect of cooling rate after sintering, sintering atmosphere and additives on the structure and dielectric Q values is assessed. Low frequency (1500 Hz) dielectric measurements of capacitance and loss factor were performed at room temperature on polished discs, using a Wayne Kerr 6425 precision component analyser. High frequency dielectric measurements were performed at 5 GHz with a network analyser and sweep oscillator, using the Hakki and Coleman method (1960).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ultrasound-a diagnostic tool for NDT of insulation degradation
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Previous work by the authors, using the techniques described, has been carried out in clear polyester resin, in order to establish the efficacy of ultrasound in the detection and location of clearly visible known imperfections in this material. Current work extends the investigation into opaque systems (filled polymers) to determine the applicability and limitations of ultrasound in more practical insulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A lightning warning device using liquid crystal elements
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Discusses an electric field sensor using a liquid crystal element for a lightning warning device, and to measure the optical transmission against the electric field strength. In this paper, two kinds of sensors, with the electrodes connected in parallel or in series, have been prepared in order to investigate its ability to detect the electric field. The performance test has also been carried out under a thundercloud to confirm the properties of the prepared sensor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The comparison of thermal imaging with the cone calorimeter for evaluating the fire hazards of electrical cables
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Small scale tests are required from which the fire hazards posed by materials or design can be judged. A number of tests are available. Thermal imaging and the cone calorimeter operated to ASTM E5, P190 shows considerable promise and the purpose of this paper is to compare the two methods and give some illustrations of their uses and show how cables can be classified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measure method for the dielectric analysis of perfluoropolyether microemulsions
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Water-in-oil microemulsions are transparent, optically isotropic, thermodynamically stable, liquid systems consisting of spherical water droplets stabilized by a surfactant shell and dispersed in a continuous hydrocarbon medium. The dielectric behaviour of such systems shows, in the frequency range (10-100)MHz, absorption phenomena caused by interfacial polarization. The authors describe a method for the determination of the dielectric parameters of highly conducting liquid dispersions exhibiting a Maxwell-Wagner absorption at frequencies where also the residual inductance contribution must be taken into account. An example of how the method works will be reported for a three-component water/oil microemulsion consisting of water, perfluoropolyether (PFPE) oil and perfluoropolyether surfactant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The checker system to provide control over gas concentration in a power transformer oil
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Gases are formed in transformer oil as a result of electrical discharge stresses and great thermal power release that causes chemical decomposition of the insulating medium. The gases formed dissolve in oil easily. Each of the main three types of faults corresponds to a specific combination of gases. With arcing discharge all gases associated with the fault are formed, pyrolysis causes the formation of all gases, except acetylene, and corona discharge causes the appearance of large amount of hydrogen. The identification of a developing fault can be performed, the severity of fault can be predicted and the time-schedule of maintenance can be determined according to the concentration of gases. The device developed is intended for the monitoring of the combustible gases' level in a transformer and is installed directly on the transformer tank or the oil cooling system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric phenomena in acrylate-butadiene-styrene terpolymer
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The aim of the authors' work is to characterize the depolarization phenomena in Acrylate-Butadiene-Styrene (ABS) terpolymer. The Thermally Stimulated Current (TSC) spectra of ABS samples have been analysed as a function of processing and printing. All samples show two intrinsic relaxation modes. The low temperature mode has been attributed to the dielectric manifestation of the glass transition of acrylic sequences. The compensation diagram can be used for defining the structure and the microstructure of the acrylic phase. The high temperature mode has been assigned to a consequence of the glass transition of the styrene-butadiene copolymeric sequences i.e. the restructuration of water molecules.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical degradation of styrene polymers
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: One problem with polymeric electrical insulation is chemical degradation under the influence of long-time electrical exposure. As a result of the resonance-stabilized aromatic ring, polystyrene exhibits relatively good insulating properties. In this work the authors present PD resistance data for well-characterized styrene polymers with various electron-donating and electron-accepting substituents.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Surface electric strength of HV insulators by partial arcs
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Presents the results of laboratory tests on the influence of partial arcs on the surface electric strength of insulators in the part which is not shunted by the partial arc. The test were carried out using 50 Hz alternating voltage for vertical and horizontal parts of insulators. The insulator consisted of an electric porcelain tube with outer diameter of 70 mm with electrodes of both big and small boundary curvature. The flashover path of the tested insulators was changed in the range from 50 to 120 mm. The length of shunted partial arc was changed in the range from 5 to 35 mm. The results of experiments and measurements indicate that there is a considerable correspondence between the surface strength of insulator and the length of shunted partial arcs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effects of additives on space charge formation in polyethylene
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The effects of additives or impurities included in LDPE on space charge formation and conduction current were studied. The conduction currents in commercially available LDPE samples are higher than that in the additive-free LDPE sample. While positive charges are observed throughout the bulk of the untreated commercially available LDPE samples, the solvent extraction treatment changes space-charge distribution to what is observed in the additives-free LDPE sample. Additives and/or impurities are thought to be the origins of mobile positive ionic carriers, which are removed by the solvent extraction treatment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Non-invasive optical fibre acoustic monitoring of partial discharges within GIS
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Although GIS were once thought to be maintenance free, there has been a number of reports of system failures throughout the world. These failures are reported to be caused by partial discharge activity within the GIS enclosure, Spaeren (1985). The authors report on a noninvasive fibre-optic technique which is shown to be sensitive enough to detect displacements of 10/sup -12/ m and has a good response at 10 kHz but can respond to signals up to 40 kHz. This optical system is a portable interferometric fibre-dyne system and can be a cost-effective, retro-fittable solution for monitoring partial discharges in GIS. Comparison with a commercially available piezo-electric acoustic emission sensor is also made.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The characterization of poly(methyl methacrylate), (PMMA), by dielectric analysis and the study of the effects of beta-alkyl substitution on the dielectric properties
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The mechanical and electrical properties exhibited by the polymethacrylates family of polymers in end-use applications are significantly influenced by the presence of relaxation transitions (alpha and beta transitions). Analyzing these transitions requires a technique that offers high sensitivity and good resolution. Dielectric analysis (DEA) can provide both of these required capabilities. Furthermore, DEA can accommodate the polymethacrylate in either film or powder form and can provide information continuously through the solid phase to well above the glass transition and into the fluid state. Dielectric analysis, which measures a material's response to an applied alternating voltage signal, provides an excellent means of characterizing thermoplastics. The actual properties monitored using dielectric analysis are e' (permittivity), which is a measure of the degree of alignment of the molecular dipoles to the applied electrical field; and e" (loss factor), which represents the energy required to align the dipoles or to move trace ions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: AC breakdown in divergent fields in mineral oil at large distances
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors present an extension of previous work in transformer oil subjected to an AC voltage in point-plane geometry at gap distance up to 25 cm. Their purpose is to study the characteristics of streamer propagation over long distances, with a view to explaining the shape of the breakdown voltage curve vs gap distance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed temperature measurement on a power cable using optical fibres incorporated in the construction
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: This paper covers work carried out by BICC Cables on a composite optical/power cable with two standard telecommunication optical fibre cables incorporated within the construction. Tests were made to assess the effectiveness of a distributed temperature sensor (DTS-80) supplied by York Sensors. This measurement technique relies on the fundamental scattering properties of an optical fibre to determine the value of temperature. The principle of operation is based on optical time domain reflectometry (OTDR).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation of pre-breakdown phenomena in polyethylene under high electric field with a streak camera
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Needle-plane geometry samples were conditioned under AC voltage in order to grow an electrical tree at the tip of the needle. Observation of the different samples under an optical microscope revealed the presence of a small electrical tree (500 mu m) at the tip of each needle. The samples were submitted to fast positive (20 ns/2 mu s) impulse voltage in the rage of 30-90 kV. Light resulting from partial discharges was emitted from the region of the electrical tree, and lasted about 20 ns. The author presents a study of double emission phenomena resulting from the partial discharges activity under fast positive impulse voltage using a streak camera. It was observed that, under some conditions, a second light emission occurs 50 ns after the first one. These phenomena were correlated to an undershoot oscillation with a change of polarity which follows the first maximum of the impulse waveform. This second light emission could be related to charge accumulation from the preceding positive impulse voltage on the surfaces of the tree branches and in the bulk of the dielectric material.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of porous materials
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors consider materials were the major contribution to the electrical conductivity is given by the pore fluid, and in particular by ionic species dissolved in it. They propose qualitative models for two main kinds of dielectric response that have been observed in porous media. Their ideas are illustrated by experimental results on cement mortars and on glass beads and sand bonded by epoxy. The electrical properties of porous materials are of importance for a range of applications. For example, oil-impregnated paper is much used as an high voltage insulation material. The breakdown strength decreases and the dielectric losses increase as the water content in the pores increases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Natural and synthetic piezoelectric materials for chemical sensors
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The coupled crystal oscillator may have the resonant frequency disturbed by the addition of mass at the crystal surface, according to the Sauerbrey relationship. The shift in frequency of the system is proportional to the mass at the crystal surface. Divinylbenzene and pyrrole polymer materials are considered in conjunction with quartz crystals. Of equal interest are a family of piezoelectric polymers based on polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF). The preparation and use of these synthetic materials is discussed alongside the naturally occurring materials, with particular reference to real-time chemical sensors. The piezoelectric material is made analyte specific by application of a surface coating doped with specific reaction sensitive molecules or ions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Photoconductivity of polymers with conjugated double bonds
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Polymers with conjugated double bonds (conductive polymers) have attracted much attention during the last ten years (1982-92) because of the possibility of producing samples with metallic conductivity by suitable dopants. Much less attention has been paid to the electrical properties of undoped samples which exhibit the electrical characteristics of insulators or semiconductors. These conditions are especially suited for the investigation of low level doping and for the measurement of the light- or radiation induced conductivity. Photoconductivity measurements are especially important since information on the charge carrier dynamics and energetics in the polymer can be obtained. Here the authors wish to report on the photoconductivity of chemically synthesized samples of polypyrrole (PPy) and polythiophene (PT). The structure formulae of these compounds are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of finite element techniques to optimise the insulation design of power transformers
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The accuracy of FE field computation now available has allowed the voltage distribution in insulation structures to be understood in detail. It is a powerful tool with which, the optimum insulation structure of a power transformer can be ensured under all types of normal and abnormal operating voltage conditions provided the correct model is created. This requires the experience of a skilled operator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Specific damage energy of dielectric materials as the universal characteristic of polymer insulation stability under the influence of surface partial discharges (phenomena, measurement, practical supplement)
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: To compare the stability of polymer insulation under the influence of partial discharges it is possible to use test results on the stability to surface partial discharges (SPD). These tests are organized in such a way that the discharges appear in the zone of triple conjugate (metal-air-polymer), as shown. The authors show that the energy parameter specific damage energy of dielectric Wp can be used as criteria of insulation stability under SPD influence where only part of SPD energy spent to damage of volume dielectric unit is taken into account. This characteristic depends only on dielectric properties. Only short time enough to damage the definite volume of dielectric is required in order to receive such characteristic.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PD scaling relationships in GIS insulators: theory and experimental verification
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) testing is commonly used as a quality control measure for epoxy insulators in gas-insulated switchgear (GIS). Occasional inservice failures have indicated that improvements to the technology should be considered. Recent theoretical developments have provided a means of assessing the detectability of partial discharges in such insulators. The theory also provides a model which can be used to relate the characteristics of voids within insulators with the measured signal and the inception/extinction voltages. The authors describe measurements which provide the experimental evidence in support of the theory. Application of the theory results in more stringent PD acceptance criteria for higher voltage class insulators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Surface flashover sustained by electrostatic surface charge on epoxy resin insulator in SF/sub 6/ (GIS insulators)
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: It has been confirmed that sufficiently high electrostatic surface charge density can sustain surface flashover when the stored surface energy released can cause further ionisation and establish a chain reaction. Therefore, in addition to the widely reported results that surface charges can aggravate the triple junction field enhancement under certain conditions, it is now clear that once triggered, surface flashover can self-propagate a long distance away from the initiation sites, resulting in unexpected and erratically low flashover voltages. The proposed self-sustained surface flashover criterion has been tested to apply for different geometries and at various SF/sub 6/ pressures. The criterion simply states that the electrostatic surface energy should be sufficient for renewed ionisation activities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermal analysis of polymeric sheathing materials for fibre optic communication cables
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: On the basis of the DSC and TGA results reported, the three commercial sheathing material were characterized as follows. The thermoplastic was found to be a linear low density polyethylene, containing approximately 5% carbon black as a UV stabilizer. The organic elastomer was identified as a cross-linked ethylene based copolymer, containing approximately 5% carbon black and 55% ATH as fillers. The behaviour of the silicone rubber was consistent with a material of this type. However, no phase transitions were evident and the decomposition behaviour and residue chemistry of these compounds is such that no estimate of filler loading could be made. From the thermal studies (DSC, TGA and laser ablation) it can be concluded that the resistance of the LLDPE to surface discharge activity should be considerably worse than that of the other two materials considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Theoretical considerations about partial discharge detection in distributed systems
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Partial discharges are localised breakdowns at low strength material or at local field enhancement sites, and may lead to a progressive total breakdown. Within high voltage power equipment they may arise at voids, contamination, poor conductor profiles and floating metal-work. A partial discharge test is, therefore, a widely used quality control test. It will be shown by the analysis in this paper, that rather than being theoretically correct, the formula given is only intuitive and offers a grossly underestimated partial discharge magnitude in all realistic circumstances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric spectroscopy of self-reinforcing polymer blends
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Dielectric measurements on blends of a thermotropic main chain liquid crystalline polymer (LCP) and an isotropic thermoplastic polymer (TP) have been carried out. Melt blending of LCPs with thermoplastic polymers often results in fibre forming of the minor LCP component during processing and hence gives a 'in situ' improvement of the mechanical properties. LCP/TP blends are therefore called self-reinforcing. The miscibility plays an important role in both the fibre formation and the improvement in mechanical properties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent advance in fine structure of water trees by confocal microscopy
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: High voltage power cables insulated with polymeric materials such as polyethylene, experience water treeing degradation produced by electrical stress in the presence of moisture. In cable insulation, the breakdown stress level is strongly affected by the size of water trees even though the treed region can be considered as insulation material. Although it is easier to observe water trees by epifluorescence with a standard microscope, the use of a confocal laser scanning microscope gives images of a better quality and allows the three dimensional reconstruction of the microchannels. Microchannels are found to grow along erratic entangling with respect to one another in three dimensions, likely according to the presence of a crystallite boundary or of heterogeneous electric field value. These diameters are less that 0.6 mu m and sometimes less than 0.2 mu m. On the basis of observations, the authors suggest that microchannels are not formed by the juxtaposition of isolated cavities, within the limit of the 0.2 mu m resolution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Water treeing in insulating liquids
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: On the assumption that water treeing activity in a heavily plasticised polymer may not differ greatly from that in a highly viscous liquid, it was decided to study the behaviour of a transparent silicone fluid interfaced with either de-ionised water or water containing 0.5 M NaCl. Alternating and direct voltages were applied to both uniform field and point-plane electrode geometries. This system allows easy optical observation and the possibility of relatively short growth times of water tree structures, so avoiding the difficulties associated with the study of water treeing in practical solid insulation such as XLPE.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Light emission studies of electrical treeing processes
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors quantitatively investigate light emission during the initiation and early growth stages of electrical treeing in CT200 epoxy and unsaturated polyester resins in order to gain insight into the underlying physical mechanisms responsible for tree initiation and growth. Ultra-sensitive photomultiplier and charge coupled device (CCD) detection techniques have been used to examine the temporal as well as spatial development of tree initiation and growth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of measuring techniques used in evaluating the insulation condition of large power transformers
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: This report illustrates the experience gained at ENEL over a 15 year period of dielectric diagnostic testing. The considerable amount of information obtained over the years from the large number of large transformers has contributed to the development of measuring techniques aimed at monitoring and inspection machines in service. ENEL performs those tests which best highlight the failure mechanisms, namely: dissolved gas in oil analysis, furfural analysis, and partial discharges measurement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental analysis of the dielectric properties of powders
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The paper is a detailed treatise on the theoretical and experimental analysis of the dielectric properties of powders. The obtained results clearly indicate that measuring the dielectric properties of powdered minerals is quite an insensitive technique (comparable with the susceptibility measurements of mineral powders as used in paleomagnetics) for which a statistical approach should be used. A combination of the random and systematic errors leads in some cases to a relative error of 10% as a guarantee limit on the estimated permittivity. Some mineral samples could not be measured in the frequency range of the experimental set-up due to relaxation phenomena.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Partial discharges using a zero cross AC voltage
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: A zero crossover AC power source has been utilised to eliminate transient overvoltages and overvoltages occurring with an increasing magnitude of applied voltage. The zero AC power source will be defined as the following; an AC power source which will produce a sinusoidal alternating voltage with a commercial frequency (50 Hz) from ground to an established peak value of the voltage. The paper presents the results of partial discharge characteristics using the zero AC voltage. In particular, the relationship between inception voltage and number of tests, and time lags is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric strength of SF/sub 6/, SF/sub 6//N/sub 2/ and SF/sub 6//CO/sub 2/ under different electrode surface conditions
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The effect of electrode surface roughness formed in the machining process can be predicted for SF/sub 6/, SF/sub 6//N/sub 2/ and SF/sub 6//CO/sub 2/ by computations using a multi-ridge surface roughness model. The breakdown strength of SF/sub 6/ gas remains higher than that of the SF/sub 6//N/sub 2/ and SF/sub 6//CO/sub 2/ mixtures (50/50) even when PR is as great as 40 kPa.mm. Only in the case of having a single large protrusion can the breakdown strength of the SF/sub 6//CO/sub 2/ mixture be slightly higher than that of SF/sub 6/ gas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of space-charge on the fracture toughness of Perspex
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Tree initiation is believed to arise from the creation of small cracks by fatigue failure, caused by cyclical electrostatic forces induced by the alternating applied voltage, with tree growth resulting from microscopic explosions, within the dielectric due to localised intrinsic breakdown on the crack surfaces. The growth appears to follow the precepts of fracture mechanics as applied to crack propagation. It is a common observation that electrical trees can fully bridge the interelectrode spacing while still retaining voltage integrity. Breakdown does not occur until the channels of the tree have widened sufficiently to sustain an electrical discharge. On the assumption that channel widening is enhanced by the repulsive forces between charges trapped on opposite faces, this paper addresses the phenomenon by first establishing the magnitude of the forces between charged dielectric surfaces.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Condition monitoring of 132 kV transformers
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Approximately 30% of the 132 kV grid transformers in the UK are over 40 years old. Some 80% are over 20 years old. Transformer loads are increasing and reserved capacities are decreasing. Consequently, it is imperative to have some simple and practical means of assessing the insulation integrity of high voltage power transformers. The objectives of the present investigation were (a) to determine an acceptable level of insulation integrity for the large population of aged transformers, and (b) to develop or implement a diagnostic technique which could be used to monitor the rate of deterioration of the oil-paper composite insulation. The degraded oil can readily be refurbished or replaced. The degradation of the insulating paper, however, is nonreversible. The effects of thermal ageing on the paper matrix are accentuated by the presence of air and moisture.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measuring moisture content in small dielectric objects of arbitrary shape
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Resonant cavity techniques are widely used in measuring the microwave properties of materials by measuring the shift in the resonant frequency and the change in the Q factor of the cavity when the object is inserted into the cavity. This technique has proven to be an interesting alternative to existing methods for kernel moisture determination in soybeans and corn, because it offers nondestructive and relatively fast measurements. The purpose of this paper is to present principles and results of research on the effect of kernels of various shapes and dimensions and different moisture contents on the parameters of a resonant cavity operating at a microwave frequency and to evaluate the feasibility for moisture content determination in individual seeds, nuts and kernels by this technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple direct life correlation based on the ageing compensation effect
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Many users who find the procedures of IEC 216 to be too complicated, may also regard the ACE equation as an additional, somewhat abstract mathematical expression. In order to respect this viewpoint and to avoid the excessive use of such concepts as Arrhenius or Eyring equations, etc., a simple new correlation is established directly between the logarithms of the measured time-to-failure (life) values.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New methods of reducing streaming current (a comparison of calculated and experimental results)
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Two well known methods of reducing streaming current are the introduction of interface activation substances and the roughening of the inner surface of the pipe wall. Numerous reports have been published on experiments concerning interface activation agents. But there have been very few experiments indeed concerning the wall surface roughening method. In addition to conducting experiments on the roughening of pipe walls, the authors have tried to discuss the factors involved in the reduction of streaming current, with the aid of solutions to Navier-Stokes equations with the use of a CRAY X-MP/14se super computer. To summarise their results, it has been found that an intimate relation exists between the streaming current and the area of pipe wall exposed to direct contact with the main path of flow in the liquid. If grooves are cut in the inner wall of the pipe, vortices occur, and since the main liquid flow then no longer comes into direct contact with the pipe wall a reduction can be observed in the streaming current.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect on DC and AC corona on the electrical properties of polymers
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: Insulation failure is a serious economic and technical problem especially in the power industry. Corona discharge phenomena, when present, appear to play an important role in the degradation of solid insulating materials. Thus the analysis of changes resulting from such degradation processes may lead to an understanding of insulation breakdown mechanisms and a more accurate determination of insulation life time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method for ranking dielectric liquids subjected to AC power voltage
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: The authors describe a test method to evaluate the breakdown properties of various dielectric liquids, with the view to determine their applicability in high voltage apparatus. The authors develop a method to characterize the properties of dielectric liquids along the following guidelines: AC voltage, moderately divergent fields of low mean values. To trigger the breakdown at such low fields, they simulate a defect by introducing a calibrated large metallic particle in the gap. This large particle constitutes obviously an oversized defect, but it allows them to reproduce several experiments in the same conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nondestructive control of dielectric plane samples in the X-band
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: A laboratory experimental set-up for detection of defects in industrial polymer plates is described. The method used is of reflexion, amplitude-phase (RAP) type. The main experimental peculiarity of the set-up is the moving microwave head in respect to the explored plate; some important conditions must be kept: strict parallelism, minimal vibrations, constant angle of exploration. The sample is set on a well polished steel desk and is explored 'line by line'. The interferential signal between the incident and reflected waves is detected and plotted as defectograms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effects of radiation and thermal ageing on physico-chemical properties of elastomeric materials (EPR-CSPE) for cable insulation and sheathing
publicationTitle: 1992., Sixth International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications
abstract: In order to estimate cable service life in nuclear power plants, a research program has been established and performed on EPR/CSPE LOCA (Loss Of Cooling Accident) cables. This program is based on study of dose (5 to 100 kGy), dose rate (10 to 2500 Gy/h) and temperature (40 to 135 degrees C) effects on these materials. This paper presents the results of physico-chemical methods (dielectric and dynamic mechanical analysis) carried out on materials after accelerated ageing to characterize the degree of degradation. Dynamic mechanical and dielectric spectra show that these materials are highly sensitive to thermal ageing, particularly CSPE. Indeed, both loss factor (tg delta ) and elastic modulus (G') are affected by temperature. Elastic modulus of the rubbery state allows crosslink densities which decrease with increasing temperature ageing to be calculated. Radiative ageing effects are the weakest. EPR is more affected than CSPE especially in the range of 30-70 degrees C where a short decrease of G', related to microcrystallinity, is modified by dose rate. Volume resistivity measurements prove higher sensibility for radiation effects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
